data.text:
Sh. Charanjeev Singh S/O Mukhtiar Singh vs Director/Controller 
on 4 November, 2024 
Author: Chief Justice
Bench: Chief Justice
 High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh
 At Jammu
 Date:04.11.2024
Wp(C) Pil No.33/2019
1. Sh. Charanjeev Singh S/o Mukhtiar Singh
 R/o H.No.28, Exchange Road, Jammu.
 .....Petitioner
 Through: Mr. Parveen Kapahi, Advocate.
 versus
1. Director/Controller
 Drugs & Food Control Organization 
 Muthi. 
2. Commissioner Municipality,
 Municipal Corporation, Jammu.
3. Assistant Director,
 Food Safety Standard Authority of India
 Fda Bhawan Kotla Road, New Delhi. .....Respondents
Through: Mr. S.S. Nanda, Sr. Aag Mr. Harshwardhan Gupta, Advocate.
Coram: Hon'Ble The Chief Justice Hon'Ble Mr. Justice M.A. Chowdhary, Judge
Oral 
1.  Through the medium of this public interest litigation, the petitioner is seeking a direction to the Director/Controller, Drugs & Food Control Organization-respondent No.1 herein to implement the Food Safety Regulations issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India- respondent No.3 herein with regard to edible and non-edible ice blocks being manufactured by such industrial units. 
2. It is averred that there are no standards for ice coming in contact with food products. Such ice Sh. Charanjeev Singh S/O Mukhtiar Singh vs Director/Controller on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192523233/
1 blocks, which come in contact with food products, are generally used for preservation, storage and transportation of perishable food commodities like cheese, meat, fish, chicken etc. It is averred that these ice bocks are manufactured un-hygienically from non-portable water which leads to contamination of food commodities which are stored/preserved or transported in such ice blocks. It is further averred that these contaminated ice blocks are also used in juices like cane sugar, cold drinks and other soft drinks by the hawkers and shop vendors, which ultimately is consumed by the common masses, as a result of which people face water born diseases and health hazards and sometime to some serious illness which even results into death. Thus, it is averred that it is the fundamental duty of the State to protect the health and lives of the citizens by taking such legal and stringent measures to prevent the use of contaminated ice blocks as the same cannot be differentiated between edible and non-edible ice for human consumption. 
3. Objections have been filed on behalf of respondents. Respondent No.2- Municipal Corporation,
Jammu has averred that the matter does not pertain to it as the Director/Controller, Drugs and Food Control Organization is the authority for food safety regulations. 
4. The present petition came to be filed in July, 2019 and the objections on behalf of respondent No.1-Drugs and Food Control Organization came to be filed in October, 2019 averring therein that the Deputy Commissioner, Food Safety & Drugs Administration, Muthi, Jammu issued a communication on 25.09.2019 requesting all the designated officers, Food Safety of all the Districts of Jammu Division to carry out special drive for one week with effect from 27.09.2019 to 04.10.2019 and take action against the manufacturers indulging in selling of non-edible ice without colour for distinguishing it from edible ice. And, as per the report received from the designated officers,
District Jammu and District Kathua, the manufacturers of non-edible ice are adding colour as per the guidelines issued by the FSSAI. Further, a public notice/advisory on edible/non-edible ice as per the guidelines issued by the FSSAI was got published in the Daily Excelsior in its issue dated 14.09.2019 and Greater Kashmir in is issue dated 06.10.2018 for the awareness of the general public including manufacturer of edible/non-edible ice. 
5. Though the grievance, as projected by the petitioner, is of grave concern, yet in view of the reports of designated officers of respondent No.1, it seems the concern raised by the petitioner in the present petition has already been addressed as, in view of the said reports, the manufacturers of non-edible ice have been adding colour as per the guidelines issued by the FSSAI so as to distinguish non-edible ice from edible ice. 
6. Therefore, we deem it proper to dispose of the present petition with a direction to the Director/Controller, Drugs & Food Control Organization- respondent No.1 herein to ensure that the order dated 25.04.2017 regarding guidelines for ice coming in contact with food products, issued by the Food Safety and Standard Authority of India, is strictly implemented in its letter and spirit. 
Ordered accordingly. However, if, at any stage, the petitioner feels that the said guidelines are being flouted by manufacturers of non-edible ice blocks, he is at liberty to approach this Court again. 
 Jammu (M.A. Chowdhary) (Tashi R  04.11.2024 Judge Chief J  (Anil Sanhotra)
